summary: Middle / inchoative voice for change-of-state transitive verbs
current_capability: nesalen is defined as transitive [Agent] nesalen [Patient-an]. Omission of object leaves role ambiguous between transitive zero-object and inchoative.
semantic_deficiency: Cannot distinguish 'X loses Y' from 'X gets lost / disappears' without an explicit voice or valency marker.
candidate_mechanism: Option A: Pre-verbal voice particle 'se' (reflexive/middle) -> 'Vel ne va se nesalen'. Option B: Verbal infix/suffix '-er-' -> 'nesaleren'. Option C: Analytical compound with state auxiliary -> 'nesal fali'.
tradeoffs: Option A is most analytic and easiest to learn; avoids morphophonemic collision. Option B increases synthetic complexity.
compatibility_impact: Additive proposal; existing transitive frames unaffected.

evidence_case: C05 (Mei ne da belemen. Mei da hüvaren)
current_capability: Verbs allow omitted arguments, but decoder has no syntactic cue whether the object is indefinite, generic, or anaphoric to a preceding clause.
semantic_deficiency: Omitted object leads to total information drop (e.g. searching for a star vs arbitrary searching).
candidate_mechanism: Option A: Dedicated neutral anaphoric object pronoun 'itan' or 'elan'. Option B: Rule licensing null object only when co-indexed in adjacent conjunct.
tradeoffs: Pronominal 'elan' leverages existing 3sg root 'eli'; minimizes vocabulary expansion.

summary: Causative voice derivation or periphrastic causative
current_capability: No causative verb morphology exists; requires periphrastic 'ke' complement clause with naelen/yelen.
semantic_deficiency: Cannot express 'make X do Y' or 'cause X to open' succinctly in literary prose.
candidate_mechanism: Periphrastic construction using matrix verb 'siren' (cause/make) + 'ke' + embedded clause.
tradeoffs: Leverages existing root 'sira' (cause/reason); zero new root required.

summary: Experiential perfect negation ('never') vs simple past negation ('did not')
current_capability: 'ne da VERBen' strictly encodes simple past negation ('did not VERB').
semantic_deficiency: Fails to distinguish episodic negation from lifetime / experiential negation ('has never in his/her life seen').
candidate_mechanism: Combine negative particle 'ne' with completed aspect 'fa' + temporal quantifier 'teli' or adverb 'orai' -> 'ne fa VERBen orai' (never completed).
tradeoffs: Uses existing aspect particle 'fa' and root 'orai' (time/occasion); transparent composition.

summary: Scope of negation over coordinate clauses and connectives
evidence_case: C07 (Mei ne da yelaren ... Mei da yelaren ...)
current_capability: Negation is strictly pre-verbal ('ne VERB'); scope does not automatically extend across sentence boundaries.
semantic_deficiency: Parallel contrastive clauses (not X, but Y) require explicit contrastive coordinators to avoid contradictory appearance.
candidate_mechanism: Formalize contrastive conjunction 'lia' ('ne X, lia Y') and clarify that 'ne' scopes only over its immediate verbal head.
tradeoffs: High clarity; prevents ambiguous wide-scope negation.
compatibility_impact: Refines syntactic interpretation without altering canonical strings.

summary: Stative predicate tense marking and state vs event distinction
evidence_case: C01 (Lüra fal ve), C10 (Meina da nivaren. Lüra fal ve)
current_capability: Verbless/prepositional predicates lack tense markers. Nominal predicates allow 'da' (past) but conflate past state with inchoative change-of-state.
semantic_deficiency: Cannot distinguish 'the door was open' (past state) from 'the door opened' (past event) or 'the door is open' (present state).
candidate_mechanism: Option A: Regularize quality derivation '-i' for all state roots -> 'fali' (open, adj), allowing 'Lüra da fali' (past state) vs 'Lüra da falen' (past event). Option B: Stative copular particle 've' with tense -> 'Lüra da ve fal'.
tradeoffs: Option A follows existing phonological pattern (Sülar -> Sülari). Highly intuitive.
compatibility_impact: Clarifies standard derivation rules without breaking v1.0 bytes.

summary: Habitual vs continuous aspect in literary narratives
evidence_case: C06 (Sira pemar el da yelen ke miraven)
current_capability: 'su' marks habitual aspect; 'du' marks progressive aspect. Pre-verbal ordering is fixed.
semantic_deficiency: Homophony between prose particle 'su' (habitual) and hyphenated semantic role 'su' (typical size).
candidate_mechanism: Strict syntax guard: isolated word 'su' preceding a verb is aspect; hyphenated '-su-' following a head noun is semantic size role.
tradeoffs: Preserves existing v1.0 standard while eliminating parser confusion.

current_capability: Only indicative mood and modal verbs ('yelen', 'naelen') exist. Counterfactual ('would have done') is unexpressed.
semantic_deficiency: Hypothetical conditionals ('if he had crossed, he would have returned') cannot be distinguished from factual conditionals.
candidate_mechanism: Modal particle combination 'da yelen' (could have) or hypothetical particle 'vo'.
tradeoffs: Particle addition vs modal verb composition.

summary: Concessive conditional ('even if') vs pure conditional ('if')
current_capability: 'şe' is the sole conditional marker ('if / eğer').
semantic_deficiency: Translating 'even if' (olsa bile) with 'şe' strips the concessive presupposition and turns an imperative urge into a conditional permission.
candidate_mechanism: Compound concessive marker 'şe-el' (literally 'if-also / even-if') or postposed 'el' -> 'Şe-el Sai vürelen, aremen'.
tradeoffs: Transparently unites conditional 'şe' and additive focus 'el' (also/even). Zero new roots needed.
compatibility_impact: Additive compound proposal; canonical 'şe' remains pure conditional.

summary: Adversative coordination ('but / yet') with clause linkage
current_capability: 'lia' is attested in v1.0 as 'ama / but', but its interaction with clause-initial subject pronouns is not fully parsed.
semantic_deficiency: Parser rejects 'lia' at clause start as unsupported coordinator.
candidate_mechanism: Extend sentence grammar to recognize coordinating conjunctions ('lia', 've') at clause boundaries.
tradeoffs: Straightforward grammar upgrade; highly natural for human speakers.

summary: Numeral and nominal plural agreement rules
current_capability: Standard documents plural '-na' and numerals (1-10), but does not specify whether 'nave' requires singular 'lüra' or plural 'lürana'.
semantic_deficiency: Inconsistency across encoders: ChatGPT used plural 'növi lürana', while other prompts used singular 'növi lüra'.
candidate_mechanism: Standard rule specification: Cardinal numbers precede the noun and take the UNMARKED singular stem ('növi lüra'), while plural '-na' is reserved for unquantified plurals ('lürana' = doors in general) or definite partitives ('nave ri lürana' = seven of the doors).
tradeoffs: Matches Turkish and Hungarian grammatical economy; reduces redundant affixation.

summary: Scope and placement of focus particle 'teli' (only/just)
current_capability: 'teli' is glossed as 'sadece / only', but its syntactic attachment (pre-nominal vs pre-verbal vs clausal) is undefined.
semantic_deficiency: Cannot tell whether 'teli' restricts the subject noun, the numeral, or the predicate.
candidate_mechanism: Constituent-adjacent focus rule: 'teli' scopes over the immediate phrase that follows it: 'teli [NP]' = only that NP; 'teli [VP]' = only performs that action.
tradeoffs: Clear compositional semantics; eliminates scope guessing.

current_capability: Only cardinal numbers (mora, davi, teli, nave...) are defined. Ordinals do not exist in v1.0/v1.1.
semantic_deficiency: Complete loss of temporal and ordinal sequencing in narratives.
candidate_mechanism: Proposed ordinal derivation suffix '-en' or particle 'ri' + number -> 'mora-ri' or 'teli-ri' / 'telina' (third). Candidate root / suffix proposal.
tradeoffs: Suffixation on numeral stems vs genitive construction 'ri teli'.

current_capability: Uninflected verbs directly modifying nouns ('lüfaren deiran') are not licensed by standard grammar. Prenominal modifiers must be qualities.
semantic_deficiency: Translators either invent illicit verbal adjectives or fail to express active/passive participles.
candidate_mechanism: Option A: Allow quality suffix '-i' on verb stems for stative/participial meanings (e.g. 'lüfari deiran' = fallen star). Option B: Relative clause with 'ke' -> 'deiran ke da lüfaren'.
tradeoffs: Relative clause 'ke' is 100% legal in existing grammar; eliminates need for new morphology.
compatibility_impact: Zero new grammar needed; stylistic guideline for translators.

summary: Spatial postposition 'lo' ambiguity: containment vs surface contact vs proximity
current_capability: 'lo' covers all locative notions (in, at, on).
semantic_deficiency: Cannot distinguish 'writing on the surface of stone' from 'writing while standing near the stone' or 'engraving inside the stone'.
candidate_mechanism: Spatial compound postpositions using existing roots: 'lo-süvar' (surface-on), 'lo-len' (inside), 'lo-nasel' (at/near).
tradeoffs: Analytical and compositional; uses existing anatomical/spatial vocabulary.

summary: Opposite directional vectors and reciprocal spatial relations
evidence_case: C08 (Davi samel da pürelen vümar ta)
current_capability: Destination postposition 'ta' indicates arrival, but cannot indicate that two entities approached from opposing poles or sides.
semantic_deficiency: Crucial poetic/philosophical nuances of convergence from opposite directions are erased.
candidate_mechanism: Propose root 'pol' / 'polar' (opposite, contrary, reverse) with spatial modifier 'pol-ra' (from opposite sides).
tradeoffs: Requires new candidate root; fulfills major expressive gap.
compatibility_impact: Provisional candidate root in proposed-lexemes register.

summary: Quotation syntax, direct discourse framing, and speech acts
current_capability: Parser rejects punctuation like quotes, colons, and question marks inside clauses.
semantic_deficiency: Direct quotation cannot be parsed or analyzed by language tools.
candidate_mechanism: Direct quotation frame: Matrix speech verb ('vesen') + colon + quoted utterance. Quoted utterance parsed as an independent inner AST.
tradeoffs: Standard linguistic design; clean hierarchical AST.
compatibility_impact: Parser extension; does not alter language morphology.

summary: Imperative / hortative mood inflection and pronoun dropping
current_capability: Verbs in isolation ('Aremen!') or with negative marker ('Ne vürelen!') are currently classified as unsupported because they lack an overt subject.
semantic_deficiency: Commands and exhortations are fundamental human language acts; currently unparseable without artificial pronouns.
candidate_mechanism: Formally license subjectless bare verb stem or infinitive as imperative / hortative speech act: 'Aremen!' (Return!), 'Ne vürelen!' (Do not cross!).
tradeoffs: Universal across natural languages; vastly improves literary and conversational naturalness.
compatibility_impact: Parser grammar extension; zero breaking changes.
